newsitem.title: NORWAY: Key Norway cabinet minister in financial scandal.
newsitem.headline: Key Norway cabinet minister in financial scandal.

text.p: Norwegian Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland called on Wednesday for a quick political solution to a financial scandal involving one of his key cabinet ministers.

Former Middle East mediator Terje Roed-Larsen, planning minister in Jagland's government, is under pressure from the opposition and media to explain new accusations linked to a 10-year-old share-option scheme.
"There must be a political solution to this matter during the day," Jagland told reporters in parliament, fuelling speculation Roed-Larsen might resign.
On Tuesday night Norwegian television suggested that for tax purposes Roed-Larsen altered key dates on documents covering the 1986 share deal.
"Yesterday evening new, serious accusations came up that make it necessary for Terje Roed-Larsen to give a public account of the situation," Jgaland said during questions in parliament.
He said Roed-Larsen would hold a news conference at noon (1100gmt).

The last two weeks have brought an avalanche of media revelations about a 600,000-crown ($95,000) share-option profit Roed-Larsen made while a marketing director at fisheries company Fideco AS in 1986.
Political analysts agreed that the scandal surrounding the man praised for helping to broker the 1993 Israel-PLO peace pact was a burden for Jagland.
"Terje Roed-Larsen is fighting desperately for his political life," said Aftenposten, Norway's most influential newspaper.

"A man who is so close to the prime minister must have water-proof integrity and credibility. The question may be asked whether Jagland can take it any more, if not Terje Roed-Larsen is dead politically," Aftenposten said.
Roed-Larsen, 48, quit as special United Nations' envoy to the Middle East a month ago to head the newly created portfolio for national planning, a key ministry in Jagland's 18-member cabinet.
Jagland's Labour minority government took office in October after the resignation of veteran premier and former Labour leader Gro Harlem Brundtland.
